bibliography.title: Mind Your Margin and Boundary: Are Your Distilled Datasets Truly Robust?

sections.title: Appendix D. Limitations and Future Work

abstract_sentences.text: Dataset distillation (DD) compresses a large training set into a small synthetic set for efficient training, but most DD methods optimize only clean accuracy and leave robustness uncontrolled.

Recent robust DD methods improve robustness, yet they often suffer from a poor accuracy–robustness trade-off because they treat all adversarially perturbed examples uniformly and do not explicitly increase inter-class separation.
We present Contrastive Curriculum for Robust Dataset Distillation (C2 R), a framework that couples an attack-aware curriculum with a contrastive robustness objective.
From a robust-margin perspective, we derive a perturbation score that approximates each sample’s robust hinge, enabling a curriculum that prioritizes the smallest-margin adversaries.
In parallel, a class-balanced contrastive robustness loss enforces adversarial invariance while explicitly widening boundary separation across classes.
Experiments on CIFAR-10/100, Tiny-ImageNet, and multiple ImageNet-1K subsets under six attacks show that C2 R achieves the best robust accuracy, outperforming prior robust DD by 2.8% on average.

experimental_design.name: datasets and task
experimental_design.description: CIFAR-10/100, Tiny-ImageNet, six ImageNet-1K subsets and later ImageNet-10; image classification.

experimental_design.name: networks and resolution
experimental_design.description: Three-block ConvNet for CIFAR and ConvNet-D4/D5 for higher-resolution data; ImageNet subsets resized to 128×128.

experimental_design.name: baselines
experimental_design.description: Main baselines are MTT, SRe2L, D4M and ROME; GUARD/RDD are described in Appendix B and RDD is evaluated under shifts.

experimental_design.name: attack protocol
experimental_design.description: Main attacks are FGSM, PGD, CW, VMIFGSM, Jitter and AutoAttack at ℓ∞ ε=2/255; Appendix adds Square, MIM, ε=4/255 and ε=8/255.

experimental_design.name: training settings
experimental_design.description: SGD with learning rate 0.01, momentum 0.9 and weight decay 5×10^-4; IPC values are 1,10,50 in prose, while Table 1 also has 5 and 30.

experimental_design.name: replication
experimental_design.description: Tables state averages over five independent runs; seed identities and dispersion are absent.

experimental_design.name: metrics and aggregation
experimental_design.description: Clean/test accuracy, attack accuracy, all-attack average robust accuracy, drop rate and accuracy versus distillation time; point estimates are averaged across runs.

experimental_design.name: controls
experimental_design.description: Component ablations use identical backbones and optimization settings at IPC=10; PGD and LS-PGD comparison uses matched four-dataset settings.

experimental_design.name: predeclared hypotheses
experimental_design.description: The introduction asks a concrete question, but experiments do not list numbered hypotheses or predeclared failure thresholds.

experimental_design.name: seeds and uncertainty

experimental_design.name: leakage audit

experimental_design.name: implementation and compute
experimental_design.description: The method gives LS-PGD/queue mechanisms and Figure 5 gives cost comparisons, but exact α, β, Z, Q defaults, hardware and full run commands are unavailable in the PDF.

final_judgment.single_storyline: C2R changes robust DD from uniform clean–adversarial alignment to smallest-margin tail optimization via AAC, then uses CRL to separate competing classes near the boundary (pp.3–6, §§4.1–4.4, ‘small robust margins’).
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body keeps the margin/hinge bridge, C2R flow, attack budgets, Tables 1–4, drop-rate/time plots, five-run aggregation and component ablations (pp.3–8).
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A–E moves pseudocode, expanded attack/baseline settings, ε/AutoAttack results, FGSM and RDD shift results, limitations and the direct margin-measurement caveat (pp.11–15).
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 problem map → Eq. (6)–(9) sortable surrogate → Figure 2 method flow → Table 3 component check links mechanism and outcome (pp.1,3–5,8).
final_judgment.largest_gap: The smallest-margin claim is explicitly an optimization interpretation, without direct margin-tail statistics, embedding separation diagnostics, uncertainty, leakage audit or full deployment protocol (pp.6–8,15).
final_judgment.transfer_rule: When failure risk is tail-dominated, share one per-example failure surrogate across scheduling, mechanism loss, ablation and evaluation rather than relying on average alignment (pp.3–6,8).
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This applies to systems with a defined threat set, sortable failure surrogate and executable outcome metric; it does not establish transfer to dense prediction, new backbones, deployment benefit, privacy or direct margin measurement (p.15).
